about: Real captures used on the marketing site: the Galley app (public/screens/ showcase, public/docs/ the docs pages' pictures, public/howto/ the how-to steps) and the Caddow example site itself (public/sites/). Every one comes from scripts/capture-screens.mjs, run against Galley built from this repository (a bundle of the CLI, given to scripts/capture/start.sh as GALLEY_CLI) with a throwaway home, throwaway copies of the fashion starter (Caddow) and the small-business starter (Lowfield, the target of the WordPress move), a stand-in Cloudflare and a stand-in WordPress site. 1440 × 900 window at 2× device scale, light appearance, the Quiet theme, no scroll bars, WebP only, with a 1× copy (<name>@1x.webp). Showcase and how-to pictures are kept under about 160 KB (quality is lowered before anything is shrunk); docs pictures keep the exact size their page declares and stay under 120 KB.
setup: Everything is in scripts/capture/: README.md has the exact steps; start.sh starts each part with a clean environment and a throwaway home (sites, host, wordpress, hosting, galley, hosted, people, stop); serve-host.mts is the stand-in Cloudflare for putting the site online.

This set shows what no release has yet, so it is taken from the repository: build the app and a bundle of the CLI (README, “Pictures of what isn't released yet”) and export GALLEY_CLI=<the bundle>. Every part below then runs the bundle; without GALLEY_CLI they run the released package.
sh scripts/capture/start.sh sites — the two throwaway sites, made with that CLI; versions are published as Tobiah Rusk <tobiah@caddow.example>, an invented person from the starter.
sh scripts/capture/start.sh host — the stand-in Cloudflare on 4791 (made-up account, caddow.example-studio.workers.dev, the zone caddow.example); prints the key it accepts.
sh scripts/capture/start.sh wordpress — the importer's stand-in WordPress site on 4792 (Fernhill Garden Studio: 12 posts, 6 pages, 2 built with Elementor).

sh scripts/capture/start.sh hosting — the stand-in Fly.io and Cloudflare for "Host the editor online" (scripts/rehearse-hosting.mjs on 4793/4794, a fake install on 4796, a stand-in Google Cloud on 4544); writes the variables the app needs to hosting.env.

sh scripts/capture/start.sh media — the stand-in bucket on 4805 (its public files on 4806) for the media-bucket step: the engine's own test fake, which checks every request's signature as R2 and S3 do. Run it before galley; it prints the key it accepts, which goes to the capture as MEDIA_KEY_ID and MEDIA_SECRET.
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=… sh scripts/capture/start.sh galley — that Galley on 4790, open on Caddow, pointed at the stand-ins; the key comes from the shell of whoever runs it and goes to that process only.
HOSTED_PASSWORD=… sh scripts/capture/start.sh hosted — a hosted install (galley serve, no site) at http://cms.localhost:4797, for its sign-in and first run.

sh scripts/capture/start.sh second — a second Galley with a home of its own, on a copy of Lowfield, on 4802: the other computer the themes step brings a theme into; its token goes to the capture as SECOND_TOKEN.

Accounts (the people step): a second hosted install with Caddow and nobody signed up — scripts/capture/README.md, “Accounts”: sh scripts/capture/start.sh people, then PEOPLE_SETUP=<its one-time Setup: link>.
Open Lowfield too (POST /api/sites/open), read both ids (GET /api/sites); the token is in the Open: line of the Galley log.
command: GALLEY_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:4790 GALLEY_TOKEN=<token> GALLEY_SITE=<Caddow id> SITE_DIR=<capture dir>/home/sites/caddow WP_SITE=<Lowfield id> WP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4792 CF_KEY=<stand-in key> HOSTED_URL=http://cms.localhost:4797 HOSTED_PASSWORD=<the throwaway password> SECOND_TOKEN=<the second Galley's token> MEDIA_KEY_ID=<the stand-in bucket's key id> MEDIA_SECRET=<its secret> PLAYWRIGHT_MODULES=<node_modules with playwright-core> CAPTURE_BUILD="built from <commit>, before <release>" node scripts/capture-screens.mjs   (no step names = the whole session in order, about an hour; with the three assistant steps left out, under ten minutes on a recent Mac)
captured: 2026-11-24, Galley 0.4.0, from bundles built from this repository, in Chromium 159.0.8154.6, following scripts/capture/README.md. Two sessions. One, built at ed3e13b and run without the three assistant steps, gave the pictures that show neither the assistant nor anything it changed (24 in screens/ and the recording, 11 in docs/, 38 in howto/). The other, built from the release commit and run whole with the assistant connected, gave the rest: every picture that shows the assistant or a change it made, the Media and Sites screens, the inbox, and the themes (17 in screens/, 10 in docs/, 22 in howto/). Assistant spend in that session: $0.48 as the app reports it (the brand read, $0.28, and three requests to the assistant). The media-in-a-bucket pictures (one in screens/, seven in howto/) are from a third session, on a fresh copy of Caddow with the stand-in bucket, from the same build. Three of those (media-bucket in screens/, steps 6 and 7 in howto/) were taken again on 2026-11-25 from Galley 0.4.2 as released (the package from npm), the same way.

notes: The session: GA4, redirects, a form field, the brand and two Search & AI fixes are each published as Tobiah Rusk, so Version history reads as one session; then three changes wait in Proof (the atelier heading in the form, the Pieces heading on the page, the campaign hero and the journal heading by the assistant) for every showcase capture; then they are published, and the site goes online on the stand-in host. Then "Host the editor online" is walked to its plan against the stand-in Fly.io (nothing created), and a hosted install started on this computer is signed in to its first run (no site connected: a hosted install only takes a repository on a code host).

search-ai first publishes a journal post that still links to /about-us/ (now redirected), so Search & AI has a certain fix to offer. Its first run of the checks usually finds the preview's pages still compiling, so it runs them twice.

The import's part-way picture (wordpress-progress, move-from-wordpress-4): the stand-in site comes over in about a second and the screen asks how far it is every 450 ms, so the screen alone rarely shows it part-way. The step reads the import's state itself and, from the first answer with posts part-way, gives the screen that same answer until the picture is taken. What the picture shows is a real answer of that import, held.

Inbox: the two visitors (Ines Marrow, Corin Vale) and the newsletter sign-up are invented, and posted to the capture address from another local address (http://localhost:8080), as a page served some other way would: from the app's own address the inbox marks a submission Test.

Where what a docs picture shows is not the size of the frame its page declares (arrange, media-generate, publish-dialog, undo-publish-dialog, proof-what-changed, and history and brand, whose columns are wider than their frames), an area of the same shape is cut and brought to the declared size. The docs' assistant reply is taken in a narrower window, narrowed until the conversation is as wide as the picture less a little room.
The dev server's toolbar is hidden in every capture, including the recording, and so are the app's passing messages (docs/inbox and add-a-form-4 are taken after “Test submission received” is closed).
Agent files are not captures: the /ai-first/ page shows this site's own files, read at build time.

Themes: the themes step makes a theme called Workroom from Quiet, exports it and brings the file into a second Galley; when it ends the first Galley is on Quiet and light again and Workroom is deleted. The grey pencil (#808080) in step 5 of the guide is typed to show the refusal, and is never saved.

Media in a bucket: nothing in those pictures is a real account. The bucket is the engine's stand-in on this computer; the account 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef, the key and https://media.example.com are made up. The capture's own Galley is started with scripts/capture/media-names.mjs, which sends its requests for those two names to the stand-in, so the screens read as they would with a real bucket. Galley itself is unchanged. The picture uploaded, spring-lookbook-cover.webp, is one of the starter's own photographs under another name. The move leaves the starter's files in the repository as well as copying them, because the starter's README and templates mention them, and the picture says so.
